sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Hibernate and JPA interview questions are a staple of every Java backend interview — the entity lifecycle, persistence context and the first-level cache, lazy vs eager fetching, the dreaded N+1 query problem and its solutions (entity graphs, JOIN FETCH, projections), @Transactional propagation, optimistic vs pessimistic locking, second-level cache, batching, and the differences between JPA, Hibernate, MyBatis and JOOQ. This page covers every Hibernate/JPA question that recurs in interviews, with code snippets and the SQL Hibernate actually emits. Expect senior interviews to dig into transaction internals and connection-pool sizing — both covered here in depth.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Three layers stacked tightly:

- **JPA spec** — entities, persistence context (1L cache), JPQL, transactions.
- **Hibernate** — implementation; flush modes, dirty checking, lazy proxies.
- **Spring Data JPA** — repository abstraction, query derivation, `@Query`.

**N+1** is always a fetch-strategy problem — solve it with `JOIN FETCH`, entity graphs, or projections.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Lazy vs eager** — default `@ManyToOne` eager, `@OneToMany` lazy. Always opt-in eager only for navigations you *always* need.
- **Entity equality** — by ID, but only after persist; for transient instances use a business key.
- **`@Transactional` propagation** — `REQUIRED` default; `REQUIRES_NEW` opens a sibling tx but only via the proxy.
- **Optimistic vs pessimistic locking** — `@Version` vs `select … for update`; choose by contention level.
- **2L cache** — opt-in (`@Cacheable`); be explicit about regions and invalidation.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"To avoid N+1 I'd use a `JOIN FETCH` query (or named entity graph) for the eager case and DTO projections for read-only paths. Transaction boundary lives at the service layer, propagation `REQUIRED` by default. For contention I'd start with optimistic `@Version` and escalate to pessimistic `for update` only on hot rows."*
